title: The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A2
main_claim: For a Hodge-generic curve C in A_2 over Qbar, only finitely many points have A_s isogenous to E1×E2 with at least one CM factor. The route is a Galois-orbit lower bound #orbit ≫ max{n^2, D}^{1/42} for mixed points, fed into Daw–Orr Thm 1.2, plus André–Oort for the both-CM case.

issues.description: The whole exponent gain depends on the period theorem having exactly the form (deg_L B)^{1/g}/||ω||^2 ≪_g [k:Q] max{1, h_F(B), log deg_L B}, with ||ω||^2 NOT inside the max. If ||ω||^2 ~ (b^2+1)y (and y can be as large as n d^3) appeared inside the max, the n^{4/3} vs n comparison in §5 would fail. I could not check the cited form against the source offline. As far as I recall the 2014 statement, the paper's form is correct.
issues.evidence: §5: n^{4/3} ≪ (b^2+1) d max{1, h_F(B), log deg} ≪ d^4·d·nd^2 needs the max to be O(nd^2). log deg_L B = log(6n^4uv) is fine, but ||ω||^2 ≪ (b^2+1)y with y ≪ nd^3 is not O(nd^2).

issues.description: Finiteness relies on Daw–Orr's conditional theorem with a complexity that is polynomially comparable to max{N(s), disc}. That comparability, and the absence of any boundary hypothesis in the corrected arXiv v4, are asserted rather than reproved. They could not be verified offline.

coverage:
Read all 6 sections in full. Checked by hand:
- Gluing lemma: the kernel lies in E[n_E]×F[n_F] with injective projections, which forces n_E = n_F; minimality of n^2.
- Tate length ℓ(A) = log|j_E|/n via functoriality of the Y×X pairing, with the torus map an isomorphism.
- Lemma rho: lattice between Λ and Λ/n, form n·H, giving the bounds 1/(n y_F) and n/y_E.
- Archimedean boundary lemma: q_u single-valued, order u^tMu, and the Schur-complement bound w^tY^{-1}w = O(1/(-log|z|)).
- Prop height: upper bound B(1 + n√D + h(j_E)/n), lower bound from the Faltings isogeny inequality, absorption for n ≥ 2A_0B; empty-boundary case via compactness.
- CM lemma: covolumes √D/2 vs y_F give b = √D/(2y_F) ∈ Z and bΛ_F ⊂ O f; Siegel plus the conductor formula give h(O) ≫ D^{1/4}.
- Threefold: membership of ω in the quotient lattice via β_i f = b f_i; deg π = n^2, deg ψ = n^4, deg_L B = 6n^4uv; ||ω||^2 = b^2u/y + b^2|τ|^2/y + v/y_F ≪ (b^2+1)y; (uv)^{1/3} ≥ y; essentiality argument (End E = Z, Hom(F,E) = 0).
- Exponent chain: y ≪ d·h(j_E) ≪ nd^3, n^{4/3} ≪ nd^7, so n ≪ d^21 and the exponent is 1/42.
- Field-degree bookkeeping and the finitely-generated-field reduction.
Not verified against sources: GR14 Thm 1.2, DO Thm 1.2 and its complexity lemmas, Lan's compactification chart statements.
sibling_notes: Family 016 companions (Abelian ZP, Elliptic Squares, Quaternionic Division) were all reported no_gap_found. Elliptic Squares states that full Zilber–Pink depends on this E×CM paper and the Quaternion paper. This paper does not cite those companions, so there is no circularity; its only external dependencies are DO, GR, Lan, Siegel and Pila–Tsimerman.
